senses.sense_definition: To divert the energy of an instinctual, primitive, or socially unacceptable impulse into a constructive, socially acceptable activity.

examples.text: He managed to <w>sublimate</w> his aggressive impulses into competitive sports.
Many artists learn to <w>sublimate</w> their personal grief into creative writing.

senses.sense_definition: To transition directly from a solid phase into a gas without passing through an intermediate liquid phase, or to cause this transition.

examples.text: Under low atmospheric pressure, dry ice begins to <w>sublimate</w> at room temperature.
The chemist heated the iodine crystals to <w>sublimate</w> them into a purple vapor.

senses.sense_definition: To deposit directly from a vapor or gas state into a solid without condensing into a liquid.

examples.text: Under freezing conditions, water vapor will <w>sublimate</w> directly onto cold glass as frost.
The hot vapors began to cool and <w>sublimate</w> onto the surface of the container.

senses.sense_definition: To elevate or raise someone or something to a high status, office, or exalted state.

examples.text: The ceremony served to <w>sublimate</w> the modest leader to the position of national hero.
He sought spiritual disciplines to <w>sublimate</w> his earthly mind to a higher realm.
The alchemist attempted to <w>sublimate</w> the base metal to remove its impurities.
Rigorous training helped to <w>sublimate</w> the raw talent of the young musicians.

traits.comment: used in archaic or literary senses

senses.sense_definition: To refine something to such an extent that it dissipates or loses practical meaning.

examples.text: Overly intricate philosophical debates often <w>sublimate</w> the real practical issues into nothingness.
The committee managed to <w>sublimate</w> the original complaint until no recognizable problem remained.

senses.sense_definition: A solid substance obtained by the cooling and condensation of a vapor produced through sublimation.

examples.text: A delicate white <w>sublimate</w> formed along the cooler neck of the flask.
The researcher scraped the crystallized <w>sublimate</w> from the condensation tube for chemical testing.
